sections.markdown:
## C2 — Confusables and KG hints, tests, permits and renewal

FACT_ID: sec03-R01 | anchor: A02
A motorcycle TIP lasts 180 days and a rider gets at most two in a 10-year period, so it bridges to the endorsement rather than replacing it. [A02]
Why it matters: group permits; difficulty medium; prereq none; confusables sec03-F12, sec03-F13 [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec03-R02 | anchor: A02
A motorcycle TIP holder must be at least 16, while the licensed motorcyclist supervising that rider must be at least 18. [A02]
Why it matters: group permits; difficulty medium; prereq none; confusables sec03-F14, sec03-F15 [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec03-R03 | anchor: A01
Interpreters may assist on every written knowledge test except commercial license tests, so a non-fluent car applicant can use one for the knowledge test. [A01]
Why it matters: group testing; difficulty medium; prereq none; confusables sec03-F05, sec03-F21 [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec03-R04 | anchor: A02
Foreign licenses from Canada, Germany or South Korea avoid the skills test, while a license from any other country requires it. [A02]
Why it matters: group testing; difficulty high; prereq none; confusables sec03-F16 [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec03-R05 | anchor: A02
Under-18 applicants need a clean record for the 90 days before the skills test, while adults instead need a TIP and possibly a 30-day practice period. [A02]
Why it matters: group testing; difficulty medium; prereq none; confusables sec03-F18, sec03-F19 [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec03-R06 | anchor: A01
The 30-day TIP practice minimum is a firm requirement on the TIP page, and the adult driver education course is only encouraged, not required. [A01]
Why it matters: group permits; difficulty medium; prereq none; confusables sec03-F09 [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec03-R07 | anchor: A03
A physician’s statement looks back six months for any loss of consciousness, while chauffeur and commercial license holders need 12 months free of blackouts, fainting or seizures. [A03]
Why it matters: group medical; difficulty high; prereq none; confusables sec03-F25, sec03-F26 [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec03-R08 | anchor: A03
Probation of at least three years is a program separate from Graduated Driver Licensing, even though teens in GDL are also on probation. [A03]
Why it matters: group probation; difficulty medium; prereq none; confusables sec03-F11, sec03-F29 [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec03-R09 | anchor: A04
A standard license runs about four years to your birthday, but an under-21 license ends on the 21st birthday no matter when it was issued. [A04]
Why it matters: group renewal; difficulty medium; prereq none; confusables sec03-F34 [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec03-R10 | anchor: A04
You may renew by mail, online or at a self-service station when allowed, but every 12 years the renewal must happen in person with a vision screening and photo. [A04]
Why it matters: group renewal; difficulty medium; prereq none; confusables sec03-F37, sec03-F38 [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec03-R11 | anchor: A03
A name change starts at the Social Security Administration and costs a fee for the new license, while an address change starts with the Secretary of State and is free. [A03]
Why it matters: group records; difficulty medium; prereq none; confusables sec03-F30, sec03-F31 [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec03-R12 | anchor: A04
A free state ID goes to drivers 65 or older only when they give up the license voluntarily, while legally blind people qualify regardless of age. [A04]
Why it matters: group renewal; difficulty medium; prereq none; confusables sec03-F40 [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0024]
